summary: ARGUS is an autonomous robotic platform for long-term (6–12 months) live observation of dividing immortalized human fibroblasts (BJ-hTERT, MRC5-hTERT) to determine whether these cells have a Hayflick limit by tracking division-rate dynamics of oldest vs. newest centriole lineages. This Technical Requirements Document (TRD v0.9b) defines functional requirements, non-functional requirements, technical solution options, pre-test data needs, and a staged work plan, with finalization to v1.0 pending biological pre-test data (V1–V6) due 03.11.2026. The project is at an early conceptual/pre-prototype stage (approximately TRL 1–2), with no experimental results yet reported and key parameters still open pending biological pre-tests.

content_blocks.title: Document Header and Version History
content_blocks.content: ARGUS TRD v0.9b, dated 2026-10-21. Status: framework; finalization to v1.0 planned for 06.11.2026, pending biological pre-test data (V1–V6). Client/biological requirements: Jaba Tqemaladze (Georgia Longevity Alliance). Engineering lead: TBD (open collaboration). Key changes from v0.9: (1) Functional requirements separated from technical solutions; (2) Microbots removed from mandatory scope; (3) New FRs added (darkness operation, situational awareness, sterile entry/exit, extension slots, minimal perturbation, 3D polarity); (4) Primary experiment goal clarified as establishing whether immortalized fibroblasts have a Hayflick limit.

content_blocks.title: Purpose, Scope, and Primary Scientific Goal
content_blocks.content: ARGUS is an autonomous robotic platform for long-term (6–12 months) live observation of dividing immortalized human fibroblasts (BJ-hTERT; cross-validation MRC5-hTERT). Primary scientific goal: establish whether immortalized human fibroblasts have a Hayflick limit (yes/no). Instrumental task: observe division-rate dynamics of the oldest-centriole (OLD) lineage vs. newest-centriole (NEW) lineage over months without opening the enclosure. Expected signal of limit onset: progressive slowing of OLD lineage relative to NEW. Context: somatic cells ≈50 divisions, stem cells ≈200, immortalized fibroblasts ≈800–1000, cancer cells several thousand. Cancer cells are a later goal only if time permits. The document covers functional/non-functional requirements, technical options, baseline + extension slots, acceptance criteria, responsibility split, and pre-test input data. Key principle: final construction rests on experimentally established requirements; parameters marked '⚠️ pre-test' are not fixed before Section 6 data.

content_blocks.title: Functional Requirements (FR) Table
content_blocks.content:
13 functional requirements defined:
- FR-1: Long-term live observation 24/7 without opening sealed enclosure; criterion ≥30 days without recording failure, then months. Status: ✅ specified.
- FR-2: Real-time mitosis detection; criterion ≥90% divisions auto-detected vs manual annotation. Status: ⚠️ pre-test (imaging rate, resolution).
- FR-3: Centriole tracking — identify mother (Cep164+) and daughter (Cep164−), age from pedigree; criterion completeness ≥80%, SNR ≥3× above background. Status: ⚠️ pre-test (critical: V3).
- FR-4: Division-rate dynamics OLD vs NEW, side by side, many generations; culture maintained as exactly 2 studied single cells; criterion statistically detectable trend. Status: ⚠️ pre-test.
- FR-5: Continuous removal of all mitotic progeny except 2 studied cells and export of debris without harming observed cells; criterion accuracy ≤2 µm, survival per V4/V5. Status: ⚠️ pre-test; method = TS (not assigned).
- FR-6: Culture maintenance (media change, reagents) without loss of containment; criterion proliferation not worse than control over 7 days. Status: ⚠️ pre-test (V6).
- FR-7 (new): Operation in complete darkness with minimal phototoxicity; criterion minimum light dose meeting SNR, 'image only when needed' mode. Status: ✅ specified (range ⚠️ V3).
- FR-8 (new): Situational awareness inside enclosure — 3D picture of activity and coordinates for safe manipulation in darkness; criterion accuracy sufficient for manipulation. Status: ✅ specified (numbers ⚠️).
- FR-9 (new): Sterile material entry and sterile waste exit over years without opening enclosure; criterion 0 contamination per entry/exit cycle. Status: ✅ specified.
- FR-10 (new): Degrees of freedom for future experiments — extension slots; criterion ≥listed slots attachable without opening mechanics. Status: ✅ specified.
- FR-11: Full digital event log + remote monitoring; criterion 100% events logged, alerts delivered. Status: ✅ specified.
- FR-12 (new): Minimal perturbation of tracked-cell position; criterion minimum compatible with imaging, 0 identity losses from perturbation. Status: ✅ specified (numbers ⚠️ V1).
- FR-13 (new): 3D cell-polarity registration (top/bottom + left/right) for future centriole-transplantation experiments; criterion orientation registered and preserved per tracked lineage. Status: ✅ specified.

content_blocks.title: Minimally Sufficient Baseline (Section 3.1)
content_blocks.content:
Baseline for first experiment (immortalized fibroblasts; OLD/NEW division-rate dynamics):
1. Sealed enclosure: 37 ± 0.3 °C; 5 ± 0.5% CO₂; 2 ± 0.3% O₂; RH ≥90% in culture volume.
2. Fluorescence imaging: 488/561 nm excitation (Centrin1-GFP / Cep164-RFP), objective + camera (selection by V3/V10, not fixed).
3. Long-term 24/7 timelapse, months of recording.
4. Mitosis detection + lineage tracking (on-device AI).
5. Centriole-age assignment by pedigree (Cep164 + lineage).
6. OLD/NEW division-rate dynamics computation.
7. Cell-removal function via swappable port (method = TS).
8. Internal cameras (day/night vision) + IR illumination + 3D map of enclosure + 3D polarity registration.
9. Sterile entry/exit transfer ports.
10. Logging, monitoring, alerts.
11. Power: UPS + LiFePO₄, ≥14 h.

content_blocks.title: Extension Slots for Future Experiments (Section 3.2)
content_blocks.content:
Future experiment extension slots:
- Additional excitation channel 640 nm and others: for other fluorophores/markers (cancer, stem); standard light port, no mechanical rework.
- Objective upgrade 40× dry → 60× water (V2): higher NA/resolution; standard holder/rail.
- Additional manipulators / in-enclosure transporter: moving vessels and tools by 3D map; standard sealed ports + control bus.
- Removal module (magnetic beads / microbots / circulation): removal method chosen after V4/V5; swappable removal port.
- Culture format change (chamber between two thin glasses, plate, dish): different protocols; standard 12×12 mm sample stage + adapters.
- Controlled fluid delivery/withdrawal: future assays; fluid port via entry transfer port.
- External equipment docking (sorting, etc.): extended protocols; exit transfer port.

content_blocks.title: Technical Solutions / Options Table (Section 4)
content_blocks.content:
Technical solution options (engineer domain, not mandates):
- FR-1/FR-3: Inverted microscope; compact optical module above sample; hybrid. Trade-off: layout, access, thermal regime. Status: open until V1–V3.
- FR-3: Objective 40×/0.95 dry (V1) → 60×/1.2 water (V2); camera RasPi HQ → sCMOS. Trade-off: SNR vs phototoxicity (FR-7) — central trade-off. Status: open until V3/V10.
- FR-5: Laser 405 nm + galvo scanner; 2 micromanipulators; fluid circulation; optical tweezers; magnetic microbeads; microbots. See companion Cell Removal Methods Comparison; joint decision after V4/V5. Status: open.
- FR-7/FR-8: Internal day/night cameras; IR illumination; stereo/SLAM 3D reconstruction. Trade-off: 3D-map accuracy vs cost/placement. Status: open (V8).
- FR-9: Sterile transfer boxes with UV cycle; sealed septum ports. Trade-off: cycle speed vs sterility assurance. Status: open.
- FR-10: Open mechanics (OpenFlexure v7 or other); standard bus/interfaces. Trade-off: maturity vs flexibility. Status: open.
- FR-11: Local LLM agent + edge AI (e.g., Hailo-8L); dashboard/Telegram. Trade-off: security/autonomy. Status: open.

content_blocks.title: Non-Functional Requirements (NFR) Table (Section 5)
content_blocks.content:
12 non-functional requirements:
- NFR-1: Positioning accuracy — stage step <100 nm. ✅ specified.
- NFR-2: Addressable-action accuracy (removal) — ≤2 µm from target. ⚠️ V4/V5.
- NFR-3: Environment stability — 37 ± 0.3 °C; 5 ± 0.5% CO₂; 2 ± 0.3% O₂; RH ≥90%. ✅ specified.
- NFR-4: Autonomy — ≥30 days without opening enclosure (extends to months). ✅ specified.
- NFR-5: Power resilience — ≥14 h (UPS + LiFePO₄). ✅ specified.
- NFR-6: Biosafety — BSL-1; BSL-2 under transduction — confirm with local committee. ✅.
- NFR-7: Optical drift — thermostable enclosure, vibration isolation; drift within focus tolerance. ⚠️ V8.
- NFR-8: Condensation — no condensate on optics/camera window over ≥14 days (37 °C, RH ≥90%); dry compartment RH <50%. ⚠️ stage 4.
- NFR-9: Licensing — Software GPLv3; hardware CERN-OHL-S v2; documentation CC-BY-SA 4.0. ✅.
- NFR-10: Budget — V1 PoC ≈$2,355 … V6 Full ≈$10,455. ✅ indicative.
- NFR-11: Culture-volume humidity — RH ≥90% at 37 °C; local dehumidification only. ✅.
- NFR-12 (new): Minimal light load — dose and number of excitations per cell per 24 h minimized while meeting SNR; 'image on demand' mode. ⚠️ V3.

content_blocks.title: Biological Pre-Test Input Data Requirements (Section 6)
content_blocks.content:
Six biological pre-tests (V1–V6) to be completed by bio-group by 03.11.2026:
- V1: Fibroblast attachment reliability and movement over 24–72 h. Output: % attached at 2/6/24 h; displacement µm/h; coating. Closes: chamber material, stage speed, autofocus (FR-1/FR-3). Deadline: 03.11.
- V2: Behaviour during division. Output: mitosis scenario (rounding/shift/attachment). Closes: tracking algorithm, imaging rate (FR-2/FR-4). Deadline: 03.11.
- V3: Real distinguishability of centriole marker. Output: SNR vs background; minimum exposure. Closes: camera/objective/filters + light load (FR-3/FR-7). Deadline: 03.11. [Critical]
- V4: Removal of a cell without harm to observed one. Output: % survival; hit accuracy. Closes: removal protocol and method (FR-5). Deadline: 03.11.
- V5: Debris/necrosis removal. Output: method; preservation of neighbours. Closes: level-2 removal choice (FR-5). Deadline: 03.11.
- V6: Effect of device environment on proliferation. Output: proliferation in chamber vs control. Closes: chamber design, lighting mode (FR-6). Deadline: 03.11.
Expected output: table 'marker → wavelength → expected intensity → recommended filters/camera → fitness criterion' + update of Sections 2–5 to v1.0 (06.11).

content_blocks.title: Engineering Verifications (Section 7)
content_blocks.content:
Four engineering verifications with defined purposes:
- V8a: XY-stage metrology. Purpose: close U-E1. Expected output: repeatability (µm), step, hysteresis. Necessity: numbers for NFR-1 and acceptance. Deadline: from 28.10, in parallel.
- V8b: Focus drift. Purpose: close U-E2. Expected output: Z drift over 24–72 h. Necessity: numbers for NFR-7. Deadline: in parallel.
- V8c: Addressable-action accuracy on inert objects. Purpose: close U-E3/U-E4. Expected output: accuracy ≤2 µm; coordination of 2 manipulators. Necessity: numbers for NFR-2. Deadline: in parallel.
- V8d: Internal cameras — 3D enclosure map. Purpose: partially close FR-8. Expected output: object-coordinate accuracy; behaviour in darkness. Necessity: safe manipulation in darkness (FR-7). Deadline: after test-stand assembly.
Note: V8 removes engineering risk (repeatability, drift, accuracy) by its own objective criteria and does NOT confirm biological fitness. Fitness established only by V10/V11 on culture.

content_blocks.title: Acceptance Criteria and Verification Methods (Section 8)
content_blocks.content:
Acceptance criteria per function:
- FR-1: Recording ≥30 days without failure; then months. Method: recording stress test. ✅.
- FR-2: ≥90% divisions detected. Method: cross-check with manual annotation. ⚠️.
- FR-3: SNR ≥3×; completeness ≥80%. Method: marker calibration on sample; spotiflow metrics. ⚠️ critical.
- FR-4: OLD/NEW trend statistically detectable. Method: pilot → power analysis. ⚠️.
- FR-5: Accuracy ≤2 µm; survival ≥specified. Method: inert (V8c) + culture. ⚠️.
- FR-7: Light load within NFR-12 while meeting SNR. Method: dose measurements at V3. ⚠️.
- FR-8: 3D-map accuracy sufficient for manipulation. Method: test-stand validation. ⚠️.
- FR-9: 0 contamination per cycle. Method: control media at each cycle. ✅ specified.
- FR-10: Slots attach without baseline rework. Method: per-slot check. ✅ specified.
- FR-11: 100% events; alerts delivered. Method: test-event injection. ✅.
- NFR-8: No condensate over ≥14 days; dry compartment RH <50%. Method: frame review (PSF), photo documentation. ⚠️ stage 4.
Acceptance rule: any item marked '⚠️' is not admitted into final specification until bio-group/verification provides the value.

content_blocks.title: Responsibility Split (Section 9)
content_blocks.content:
Bio-group (J. Tqemaladze): biological hypothesis, pre-tests (§6), measurable requirements, success criteria, culture validation. Excludes: engineering decisions, component selection.
Engineer: concept, alternative technical solutions, mechanics, electronics, software, calibration on inert objects, assembly. Excludes: biological conditions and predictions; final construction only per TRD data.
Joint: TRD v1.0, final optics selection, removal method, acceptance, grant application.

content_blocks.title: Work Order / Staged Plan (Section 10)
content_blocks.content:
Staged work plan:
- Stage 0: Biological pre-experiments (V1–V6). Responsible: Bio-group. Deadline: 27.10–03.11.2026.
- Stage P (parallel): Metrology (V8), concept, software modules, calibration on inert objects. Responsible: Engineer. Deadline: from 28.10, not blocked.
- Stage 1: TRD v1.0 (finalize Sections 2–5 from stage-0 data). Responsible: Joint. Deadline: 06.11.2026.
- Stage 2: Optics/camera/filters and removal-method selection per TRD v1.0. Responsible: Engineer (per TRD). Deadline: after 06.11.
- Stage 3: Mechanics construction, electronics, software integration. Responsible: Engineer. Deadline: per plan.
- Stage 4: Culture validation against Section 8 criteria. Responsible: Joint. Deadline: when ready.

content_blocks.title: Risks and Open Questions (Section 11)
content_blocks.content:
Key risks identified:
1. Marker SNR below threshold (V3) → more sensitive camera / longer exposure / alternative marker. Open until V3.
2. SNR ↔ phototoxicity conflict (FR-7): more light = better tracking but higher risk over months. Central trade-off of stage 1; resolved by V3 + 'image on demand' mode.
3. Cell drift beyond tracking capability (V1/V2) → autonomy limits. Open.
4. Survival at removal below threshold (V4) → revise criterion/method. Open.
5. 3D-map accuracy of internal cameras insufficient for manipulation in darkness → constrains FR-8. Verified by V8d.
6. Transfer-port sterility (FR-9) — control media each cycle; risk revealed at validation.
7. Condensation on sCMOS at RH ≥90% — hermetically sealed, desiccated sensor chamber mandatory (NFR-8, §12).
8. BSL-2 under transduction — confirm with local committee.
9. Grant application: functions as 'goals + validation plan + success criteria'.

content_blocks.title: Humidity Management in the Enclosure (Section 12)
content_blocks.content:
Problem: culture volume requires RH ≥90% at 37 °C (otherwise media evaporation and osmolarity drift). Humid air over months causes condensate on cooled sCMOS sensor (down to −20 °C), cold spots (Peltier, heatsinks), objective body, and mould. Dew point at 37 °C / RH 90% ≈35 °C — any surface colder will condense.
Protection scheme:
1. Hermetically sealed, desiccated sCMOS sensor chamber — mandatory.
2. Camera-window heating (≈2–5 W, ~38 °C — above dew point).
3. Dry instrument compartment (sealed partition between humid culture volume and dry instrument volume; 3Å molecular-sieve cartridge, target RH <40–50%).
4. Local purge with dry filtered air (HEPA H14) into dry compartment; NOT N₂ (interferes with O₂ control).
5. Thermal decoupling and objective heating (components in humid volume held ~37 °C).
6. Monitoring and alerts (T/RH sensor in dry compartment; alert at RH >50%).
Acceptance criterion (NFR-8): ≥14 days at 37 °C / RH ≥90% — no condensate/frost on camera window and optics; dry compartment RH <50%.
Open decision for engineer (before stage 3): combine items 2–4 within budget and layout. Item 1 is mandatory in any variant.

content_blocks.title: Cell Lines and Scientific Context
content_blocks.content: Cell lines: BJ-hTERT (primary), MRC5-hTERT (cross-validation). Both are immortalized human fibroblasts. Fluorescent markers: Centrin1-GFP (centriole marker) and Cep164-RFP (mother centriole marker, Cep164+). Centriole age assignment by pedigree: Cep164+ = mother (oldest), Cep164− = daughter (newest). Scientific context: Hayflick limit — somatic cells ≈50 divisions, stem cells ≈200, immortalized fibroblasts ≈800–1000, cancer cells several thousand. The experiment design maintains exactly 2 studied single cells (OLD and NEW centriole lineages) by continuously removing all other mitotic progeny. Biosafety: BSL-1 baseline; BSL-2 under transduction (lentiviral/retroviral for fluorescent marker introduction). Budget range: V1 PoC ≈$2,355 to V6 Full ≈$10,455. Open-source licensing: GPLv3 (software), CERN-OHL-S v2 (hardware), CC-BY-SA 4.0 (documentation).

key_findings: ARGUS is a pre-prototype autonomous robotic platform (TRL 1–2) with no experimental results yet; all key biological parameters are pending pre-test data (V1–V6) due 03.11.2026.

Primary scientific goal: establish whether immortalized human fibroblasts (BJ-hTERT, MRC5-hTERT) have a Hayflick limit by tracking division-rate dynamics of oldest (OLD) vs. newest (NEW) centriole lineages over 6–12 months.
Cell lines: BJ-hTERT (primary) and MRC5-hTERT (cross-validation); fluorescent markers Centrin1-GFP and Cep164-RFP for centriole identification.

Key functional requirements include: ≥90% mitosis detection (FR-2), centriole tracking completeness ≥80% with SNR ≥3× background (FR-3), cell removal accuracy ≤2 µm (FR-5), 0 contamination per sterile entry/exit cycle (FR-9), and ≥30 days continuous recording (FR-1).
Environment specifications: 37 ± 0.3 °C; 5 ± 0.5% CO₂; 2 ± 0.3% O₂; RH ≥90% in culture volume; stage positioning accuracy <100 nm (NFR-1).
Central technical trade-off: SNR vs. phototoxicity (FR-7/NFR-12) — more light improves centriole tracking but risks cell viability over months; resolved by V3 pre-test + 'image on demand' mode.
Biosafety: BSL-1 baseline; BSL-2 under transduction — local committee confirmation required.
Budget range: V1 PoC ≈$2,355 to V6 Full ≈$10,455; open-source licensing (GPLv3/CERN-OHL-S v2/CC-BY-SA 4.0).
Engineering lead is TBD; client is Georgia Longevity Alliance (J. Tqemaladze); grant application is planned using this TRD as goals + validation plan + success criteria.
Microbots demoted from mandatory scope to one option among several for cell removal; removal method to be decided jointly after V4/V5 pre-tests.

Condensation risk on sCMOS sensor (cooled to −20 °C) in high-humidity enclosure (RH ≥90%, 37 °C) identified as a critical engineering challenge; hermetically sealed desiccated sensor chamber is mandatory.
No experimental data reported in this document; all results are pending future pre-tests and engineering verifications.
